t: You're standing where the London Coal Exchange once stood, on the north side of Thames Street, nearly opposite Old Billingsgate Market. The building you'd have seen here, opened by Prince Albert in October 1849, was one of the first substantial buildings made from cast iron, built several years before the hall at the Great Exhibition. It was designed by James Bunstone Bunning, architect to the City of London from 1843 until his death. It was demolished in 1962 to widen the road, despite a Victorian Society campaign. Its cast iron inspired the dragon boundary marks at the City's entrances.
